articles.title: From Udupi to the Pacific Northwest: Hari Nayak Plots Indian Cuisine's Next Frontier
articles.excerpt: The Michelin-recognised chef is opening a new restaurant at Woodinville's Harvest Yard that filters India's culinary traditions through the bounty of the Pacific Northwest.
articles.image_caption: Tandoori chicken served with herb rice, showcasing modern Indian fine-dining presentation
articles.nri_angle: A Michelin-star Indian chef opening in the Pacific Northwest gives the large Seattle-area Indian American community a fine-dining destination that redefines Indian cuisine beyond neighbourhood curry houses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Butter Chicken at Costco: How Indian Food Brands Are Storming America's Grocery Aisles
articles.excerpt: From Quicklly's launch at 2,500 ALDI stores to Truly Indian's NEXTY Award nods, packaged Indian cuisine is muscling into mainstream American retail at an unprecedented pace.
articles.image_caption: Butter chicken served with naan and garnished with cilantro, now a mainstream American grocery staple
articles.nri_angle: Butter chicken and tikka masala naan at Costco and ALDI represent a cultural milestone for Indian Americans who have long wished for their staple foods in mainstream American grocery stores.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Copper and Courage: How a Punjabi Family Rebuilt Their Las Vegas Restaurant and Earned a James Beard Nod
articles.excerpt: When the Dhillon family's beloved Indian restaurant was demolished with the Hawaiian Marketplace, their son brought it back — and in its first year, Tamba became a James Beard Best New Restaurant finalist.
articles.image_caption: An Indian dinner spread at a restaurant, featuring curry, rice, and traditional accompaniments
articles.nri_angle: The Dhillon family's journey from Punjabi immigrants running a small Monterey restaurant in 1989 to James Beard Best New Restaurant finalists in Las Vegas mirrors the broader Indian American story of ambition and cultural pride.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Chicago's Michelin Star to Phoenix and Hudson Yards: The Sujan Sarkar Playbook
articles.excerpt: The Kolkata-born chef behind Indienne is building a multi-city, multi-concept Indian restaurant empire — and mentoring the next generation of desi chefs along the way.
articles.image_caption: The Michelin Guide — Chef Sujan Sarkar's Indienne in Chicago holds a coveted Michelin star (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian American chef Sujan Sarkar is building what may become the first Michelin-scale Indian restaurant empire in the US, proving that desi cuisine belongs at every level of American dining.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Chai Just Got Cheaper: India Wins Zero-Duty Tea Access to America
articles.excerpt: A tariff breakthrough gives Indian tea exporters an edge over China just as a wave of Asian tea brands floods the US market.
articles.image_caption: A glass of freshly brewed masala chai served in a traditional Indian style
articles.nri_angle: Zero-duty tariffs on Indian tea could make authentic chai more accessible and affordable for NRIs while helping Indian brands compete against Chinese tea chains flooding the US market.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mango Diplomacy: How India's Embassies Are Making America Fall for the King of Fruits
articles.excerpt: From Costco aisles to Dupont Circle tents, Indian mangoes are selling out faster than they arrive — powered by NRI nostalgia and a quiet diplomatic push.
articles.image_caption: Ripe mangoes, whole and halved, showing golden flesh
articles.nri_angle: For 4.8 million Indian Americans, Indian mangoes are an annual emotional lifeline to home — and now embassies and Costco are making them accessible.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Quiet Rise of the Biryani Belt: How One Franchise Built 50 Outposts Across America
articles.excerpt: Bawarchi Biryanis, run almost entirely by Telugu-American families, has become the largest Indian restaurant franchise in the US — and just opened inside a Colorado hotel.
articles.image_caption: A plate of mutton biryani served with accompaniments
articles.nri_angle: The Bawarchi franchise story is the Telugu-American diaspora story — families bringing Hyderabadi biryani to every American metro where their community has settled.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Michelin Stars to Street Rolls: Indian Restaurants Claim New American Ground
articles.excerpt: A wave of openings — from a James Beard semifinalist in Phoenix to Kolkata street food in Jersey City — signals that Indian cuisine's US expansion is accelerating faster than ever.
articles.image_caption: An elaborate spread of regional Indian dishes — from Michelin-starred restaurants to street-food icons, Indian cuisine is claiming new ground across America (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian restaurants are no longer clustering in coastal enclaves — they're planting flags in Phoenix, Fort Collins, and the Hudson Valley, following the diaspora into America's interior.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Grandma's Haldi, America's 'Herb of the Year': Turmeric's Golden Coronation
articles.excerpt: The International Herb Association has named turmeric its 2026 Herb of the Year, a recognition that would surprise exactly zero Indian grandmothers.
articles.image_caption: Vibrant turmeric powder spelled out in golden yellow on a dark surface
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up with haldi doodh as the cure for everything, watching turmeric become a $1 billion wellness ingredient in the West is both validating and a little surreal.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Doubles, Bunny Chow, and Idli Shrimp: Drāvida Maps the Diaspora's Forgotten Food Routes
articles.excerpt: Chef Aarthi Sampath's new East Village restaurant doesn't just serve Indian food — it traces how Indian flavours migrated across the Caribbean, Africa, and Southeast Asia.
articles.image_caption: A golden crispy masala dosa served with coconut chutney and sambar
articles.nri_angle: Drāvida's menu is a mirror for NRIs: it asks what happens to food when people migrate, and whether the dishes that evolved in Trinidad, South Africa, and Malaysia are as 'Indian' as the originals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Beyond Tikka Masala: Kerala's Coconut-and-Curry-Leaf Cuisine Stakes Its Claim in America
articles.excerpt: Datassential named Keralan food a 'Cuisine to Know for 2026' as coconut-forward South Indian restaurants multiply across major U.S. metros.
articles.image_caption: Appam, a soft fermented rice pancake, served with a coconut-milk vegetable stew, a classic Kerala breakfast.
articles.nri_angle: For Malayali and South Indian families abroad, seeing home-state dishes like appam, stew and the banana-leaf sadya celebrated at buzzed-about U.S. restaurants is a long-awaited vindication.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Patel Brothers Effect: America's Largest Indian Grocer Bets on the Suburbs
articles.excerpt: As the chain breaks ground on new suburban megastores, NRI grocery demand is shifting from basic staples to region-specific snacks, festival sweets and Ayurvedic goods.
articles.image_caption: A Patel Brothers store in Hicksville, New York; the chain is America's largest Indian grocer (Wikimedia Commons).
articles.nri_angle: A new Patel Brothers within driving distance spares NRI families long pilgrimages to big-city Indian quarters and signals their suburb has hit a demographic tipping point.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The British Are Coming, Bearing Black Dal
articles.excerpt: A wave of London's most celebrated Indian restaurants is crossing the Atlantic to New York, betting that America is finally ready for the cuisine Britain has loved for decades.
articles.image_caption: A bowl of Punjabi-style dal makhani, the slow-cooked black lentil dish that has become a signature of British-Indian dining.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs in the US who once envied London's Indian dining scene, the arrival of Dishoom, Ambassadors Clubhouse and Darjeeling Express closes a decades-long gap across the Atlantic.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Makhana's American Moment: The Lotus Seed Taking On Popcorn
articles.excerpt: Once a humble fasting snack from the ponds of Bihar, roasted fox nuts are riding India's protein and clean-label boom into American pantries and Amazon best-seller lists.
articles.image_caption: Makhana (fox nuts) roasted with masala and ghee, the traditional Indian preparation now being sold flavored and ready-to-eat in the West.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs, makhana is the taste of grandmother's kitchen and fasting-day snacks — now it is showing up on American supermarket shelves as the latest health-food darling.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Aam, Sago and the Summer of the Viral Desi Dessert
articles.excerpt: From mango sago to ragi lava cake, India's home cooks and chefs are turning peak mango season into a parade of internet-breaking sweets — and the diaspora is reaching for the blender.
articles.image_caption: A chilled glass of mango lassi, the classic summer drink reinvented this season in viral panna cotta and sago forms.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs far from India's mango season, these viral recipes are a way to recreate the taste of an Indian summer in a Western kitchen, one blender batch at a time.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
